Recent exchange of missiles between Iran and Israel highlights diverging views between US president and Israeli PM The latest eruption of hostilities between Iran and Israel appears to have been contained for now after Donald Trump insisted he called “all the shots” in the Middle East, but in a dangerously fragile region Benjamin Netanyahu has again shown he is ready to take shots of his own. The exchange of missiles on Sunday and Monday was ample demonstration of the inherent instability of the current limbo between war and peace, but it also shone a bright light on the complex and conflicted relationship between the US president and the Israeli prime minister, frenemies who could determine the fate of the current ceasefire. Trump went out of his way on Sunday to stress that he was the dominant partner in the relationship.

In a statement, the Red Cross said "the targeting that occurred in front of the Lebanese Red Cross center in Tyre" wounded four paramedics. Lebanese state media had earlier reported an Israeli strike on a vehicle in front of the facility. President Trump called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday, a White House official told AFP, after the first exchanges of fire between Israel and Iran since a ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran came into effect in early April. The call came amid reports of an increasingly testy relationship between the U.S. leader and Netanyahu, with Mr. Trump calling his ally "f****ng crazy" during another recent phone call between the two, according to Axios.

Trump routinely uses public humiliation in response to any perceived insubordination. Against Netanyahu, it worked for less than a week. After a string of Israeli casualties in Lebanon over the weekend, the prime minister ordered the bombing of the Hezbollah stronghold in the southern Beirut district of Dahiyeh on Sunday, triggering a salvo of Iranian missiles aimed at Israel in response. Despite managing to intercept the incoming projectiles and Trump’s urging not to retaliate, Netanyahu ordered a response in kind: missile strikes against targets in Iran. The exchanges spilled into Monday morning before both sides declared a halt so Trump could declare the ceasefire back on track, with a blockade kept in place on the strait of Hormuz, “until a ‘Final Deal’ is reached.

The latest eruption of hostilities between Iran and Israel appears to have been contained for now after Donald Trump insisted he called “all the shots” in the Middle East, but in a dangerously fragile region Benjamin Netanyahu has again shown he is ready to take shots of his own.

The exchange of missiles on Sunday and Monday was ample demonstration of the inherent instability of the current limbo between war and peace, but it also shone a bright light on the complex and conflicted relationship between the US president and the Israeli prime minister, frenemies who could determine the fate of the current ceasefire.

Trump went out of his way on Sunday to stress that he was the dominant partner in the relationship.

“I call all the shots. He doesn’t call the shots,” he told the Financial Times. Less than a week earlier, the White House had leaked details of a foul-mouthed tirade from Trump, telling Netanyahu he was “crazy”, suggesting he did not know what he was doing, and informing him “everybody hates you now”.

The tongue-lashing was reportedly aimed at warning Netanyahu against attacking Beirut in his pursuit of Hezbollah, a red line for Iran in terms of what it considered a violation of the broader regional ceasefire.

Trump routinely uses public humiliation in response to any perceived insubordination. Against Netanyahu, it worked for less than a week. Despite managing to intercept the incoming projectiles and Trump’s urging not to retaliate, Netanyahu ordered a response in kind: missile strikes against targets in Iran. payload.title: Trumpin ja Netanjahun jännitteet koettelevat Lähi-idän tulitaukoa
payload.summary: Iranin ja Israelin tuore ohjusvaihto on saatu toistaiseksi pysäytettyä, mutta tapahtumat nostivat esiin Donald Trumpin ja Benjamin Netanjahun kiristyneen suhteen sekä tulitauon haurauden.
payload.content:
Iranin ja Israelin sunnuntaina ja maanantaina käymä ohjusvaihto näyttää toistaiseksi rauhoittuneen, mutta se paljasti jälleen, kuinka hauras Lähi-idän tulitauko on. Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump on korostanut johtavaa rooliaan alueella, samalla kun Israelin pääministeri Benjamin Netanjahu on osoittanut olevansa valmis omiin sotilaallisiin ratkaisuihinsa.

## Tulitauko pysyi vain vaivoin raiteillaan

Tuore yhteenotto oli ensimmäinen Israelin ja Iranin välinen tulenvaihto sen jälkeen, kun Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin välinen tulitauko tuli voimaan huhtikuun alussa. Valkoisen talon edustajan mukaan Trump soitti Netanjahulle maanantaina tilanteen kärjistyttyä.

Jännitteet kasvoivat viikonlopun jälkeen, kun Israelissa oli raportoitu tappioita Libanonissa. Netanjahu määräsi sunnuntaina iskun Hizbollahin tukialueelle Dahiyehiin, joka sijaitsee Beirutin eteläosassa. Tämän jälkeen Iran laukaisi ohjuksia kohti Israelia. Israel onnistui torjumaan saapuvia ohjuksia, mutta Trumpin vetoomuksista huolimatta Netanjahu määräsi vastaiskuja Iranissa sijaitseviin kohteisiin.

Tulenvaihto jatkui maanantaiaamuun ennen kuin molemmat osapuolet ilmoittivat sen päättyneen. Tämän jälkeen Trump saattoi todeta tulitauon olevan jälleen raiteillaan. Samalla Hormuzinsalmen saarto jäi voimaan siihen asti, kunnes lopullinen sopimus saavutetaan.

## Johtajien suhde varjostaa kriisinhallintaa

Tapahtumat korostavat Trumpin ja Netanjahun vaikeaa suhdetta. Trump on julkisesti painottanut, että hän määrää Lähi-idän linjan, ja hän pyrki sunnuntaina tekemään selväksi olevansa kaksikon vahvempi osapuoli. Netanjahun toiminta kuitenkin osoitti, ettei Israelin pääministeri ole valmis sitomaan ratkaisujaan kokonaan Washingtonin tahtoon.

Suhteen kerrotaan kiristyneen viime aikoina. Axiosin mukaan Trump oli kutsunut Netanjahua erittäin karkealla ilmauksella aiemmassa puhelussa. Samalla alueen laajempi turvallisuustilanne pysyy levottomana: Libanonin Punaisen Ristin mukaan neljä ensihoitajaa haavoittui Tyren keskuksen edustalla tapahtuneessa iskussa, josta Libanonin valtiollinen media oli aiemmin kertonut Israelin iskuna ajoneuvoon.

Tulitauko on siis voimassa, mutta sen kestävyys riippuu paitsi Iranin ja Israelin toimista myös siitä, pystyykö Trump pitämään Netanjahun linjan omansa mukaisena.
